cta.title: Stop Searching for Software. Get Schedules Done.
cta.description: Book a call to talk through your scheduling needs and learn how Scheduling Wizard works. Join 30+ departments across 20+ hospitals and practices that have us build their call, block, clinic and shift schedules.

faq.answer: Physician scheduling software typically refers to self-service tools that require your team to learn, configure, and operate a platform. Scheduling Wizard takes a different approach entirely: it is a managed service where your program submits its rules and receive finished schedules, built to your rules, delivered as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you. There is no software for your team to learn or maintain. This done-for-you model eliminates the operator burden from chief residents and coordinators entirely.
faq.question: What is physician scheduling software and how does Scheduling Wizard differ?

faq.answer: We build the ACGME requirements in as the schedule is created rather than checking it afterward: the 80-hour weekly limit, minimum rest requirements, the 24-hour cap, and the specialty-specific Program Requirements for your program. We work from the requirements your program tells us apply, and we redraft when something needs to change. Groups and practices outside GME have no ACGME requirement, so for them we build to their own rules instead.
faq.question: How do you handle ACGME requirements for a residency or fellowship?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard delivers four types of schedules: Block and rotation schedules, Call schedules with fairness optimization, Clinic schedules, and Attending physician schedules. All schedule types are built together, so changes in one schedule automatically propagate across the others without manual cross-referencing.
faq.question: What types of physician schedules does Scheduling Wizard produce?

faq.answer: Yes. Many Scheduling Wizard clients continue using the platform they already have for day-to-day schedule access. Scheduling Wizard handles the schedule creation and optimization, delivering finished schedules as Excel or Google Sheets, or on a custom live view we build for you that your team can upload directly into your existing viewing platform. The two workflows are complementary, not mutually exclusive.
faq.question: Can Scheduling Wizard work alongside the tools you already use?

faq.answer: The subspecialty requirements you tell us apply are built in too. Rather than applying a generic compliance checklist, our team applies the specific duty hour rules, rotation requirements, and call restrictions relevant to your program's specialty. ACGME compliance is the most common question on sales calls, and it is designed to be answered with confidence for each specific subspecialty.
faq.question: How does Scheduling Wizard handle subspecialty-specific ACGME scheduling rules?

faq.answer: Scheduling Wizard handles mid-year revisions as part of the managed service. When changes arise due to sick leave, parental leave, schedule swaps, or new rules, the affected portions of the schedule are rebuilt without disrupting the entire published schedule. Programs submit the updated rules and receive a revised schedule back, without needing to manually patch a spreadsheet or re-enter data into a software platform.

I'm a program director looking for a replacement for our current scheduling method because it's too complicated and doesn't handle our specific subspecialty needs, leading to conflicts and gaps in coverage.
As a program coordinator, I want a way to automate the schedule generation process so I can save time and avoid constant back-and-forth with my team over scheduling disputes and compliance issues.

I manage a private practice and need a solid scheduling solution that not only handles physician availability but also integrates with my existing tools, unlike what's currently available in generic scheduling software.
